shortDescription: Chicago Board of Trade soybean futures dipped on Thursday as traders waited to see whether Chinese President Xi Jinping's visit to the White House would boost China's demand for US supplies.

children: Chicago Board of Trade soybean futures dipped on Thursday as traders waited to see whether Chinese President Xi Jinping's visit to the White House would boost China's demand for US supplies.
US President Donald Trump welcomed Xi to the White House for a lavish state summit expected to be heavy on symbolism but light on substance
Some grain traders were growing impatient about the lack of concrete news about trade deals from the summit

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told Fox News on Wednesday after talks with Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng that they had agreed to extend until January 10 an agreement that paused a trade war that saw mutual tariffs top 100%
Private exporters reported sales of 120,000 metric tons of US soybeans to China, the US Department of Agriculture said in its daily reporting system
USDA said net US soybean export sales in the week ended September 17 were 582,400 metric tons for shipment in the current marketing year, below trade expectations
CBOT November soybeans (SX26) closed down 1/2 cent at $13.17-1/2 per bushel
CBOT December soymeal (SMZ26) jumped $1.80 to $372.40 per ton and set a contract high
CBOT December soyoil (BOZ26) fell 0.26 cent to close at 67.55 cents per pound and touched the lowest level since August 27
